title: Expected-time randomized decision implies polynomial-time verification
statement: Let $L$ be a language of bit strings. If a finite nondeterministic Turing machine decides membership in $L$ with acceptance probability at least $2/3-\varepsilon$ for every positive rational $\varepsilon$, and for every input its sum of probabilities of not having halted by each time up to any finite cutoff is bounded by a polynomial in the input length, then there is a polynomial-time randomized verifier whose acceptance probability is at least $2/3$ on members of $L$ and whose rejection probability is at least $2/3$ on nonmembers.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ belongs to the class defined as the union, over exponents $e\in\mathbb N$, of languages decided by a finite nondeterministic Turing machine
For some constant $c\in\mathbb N$, each input's cumulative sum of probabilities of not having halted over every finite time range is at most $c(n^e+1)$
For every input and every positive rational $\varepsilon$, the probability of halting with the correct one-bit membership output is at least $2/3-\varepsilon$
